newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURK VESTEL TO OFFER NEW SHARES TO FOREIGN FUNDS.
newsitem.headline: TURK VESTEL TO OFFER NEW SHARES TO FOREIGN FUNDS.

text.p: Turkish consumer electronics producer Vestel Elektronik Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. said it would offer 750 million new shares to foreign funds when raising its capital to four trillion lira from 559.845 billion.
Vestel expects an income of around $40 million from the public offer, to be used in financing capacity increase and modernisation investments, the company said in a statement.

It said the public share in Vestel which is largely owned by the Turkish textile, electronics and tourism group Zorlu Holding is expected to rise to around 33 percent after the offer from the current 18 percent.
The capital increase is subject to approval by the regulatory Capital Markets Board. The offer will be managed by Turkiye Sinai Kalkinma Bankasi.

The company plans to raise its capital to four trillion lira by issuing 890.155 billion lira of bonuses, or 1.59 bonus for one existing share and 2.55 trillion lira worth rights. It will waive 750 billion lira of the preemptive rights to sell them to foreign investors.

The remaining 1.8 trillion lira of rights, or 3.215 rights for one existing share will be distributed to shareholders. Almost all firms listed on the Istanbul Stock Exchange exercise rights at 1,000 lira nominal value per share.
Vestel Elektronik produces television and music sets, monitors, video cassette recorders.
It aims to produce two million TV sets this year after one million sets in 1996 when its domestic market share stood at 40 percent. Its share in Turkish exports of TV sets was 60 percent last year.
Zorlu Holding bought state Denizbank for $66 million from the privatisation administration OIB in a sell-off tender in January.
